'''Richard Samuel Ward''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 6 September 1951) is a British [[mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]]. He is a Professor of Mathematical & Theoretical Particle Physics at the [[University of Durham]].<ref>[https://www.dur.ac.uk/research/directory/staff/?mode=staff&id=481 Staff profile], University of Durham, retrieved May 14, 2022.</ref>

== Work ==
Ward earned his Ph.D. from the [[University of Oxford]] in 1977, under the supervision of [[Roger Penrose]]. He is most famous for his extension of Penrose's [[twistor theory]] to nonlinear cases, which he with [[Michael Atiyah]] used to describe [[instanton]]s by vector bundles on the three-dimensional complex [[projective space]]. He has related interests in the theory of [[Monopole (mathematics)|monopoles]], [[topological]] [[solitons]] and [[skyrmions]].

==Honors and awards==
Ward was awarded the [[Whitehead Prize]] in 1989 for his work in mathematical physics.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20160328124644/http://blms.oxfordjournals.org/content/22/1/109.full.pdf Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society], retrieved 2016-02-27.</ref> He was elected as a fellow of the Royal Society of London in 2005.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200508/people.pdf Notices of the AMS - Sept 2005] [[American Mathematical Society]]</ref> His certificate of election reads: {{centered pull quote|Richard Ward is distinguished for pioneering and elegant research in mathematical physics. He adapted the [[twistor transform]] to the [[Duality (mathematics)|self-dual]] [[Yang–Mills theory|Yang-Mills]] (SDYM) equation, and with Atiyah constructed general multi-instanton solutions. His discovery of the toroidal [[BPS monopole|BPS two-monopole]] was a breakthrough in [[soliton]] theory. He showed that virtually all known [[Integrable system|integrable equations]] arise from SDYM by dimensional and algebraic reductions, allowing a unified solution method. Ward's twistor transform of SDYM, applied to [[string theory]], is leading to striking progress in quantum Yang-Mills theory.<ref name="frsCitation">{{cite web|url=https://catalogues.royalsociety.org/CalmView/Record.aspx?src=CalmView.Catalog&id=EC%2F2005%2F41|title=Ward, Richard Samuel: certificate of election to the Royal Society|publisher=[[The Royal Society]]|accessdate=20 December 2025 }}</ref>}}
